# myboard

> myboard is a small self-hosted task tracker: projects with a kanban board of tasks, notes and labels, and a discussion under each task with reactions and files. This file is the complete guide to its HTTP API for scripts and AI agents. The API is the standard PocketBase REST API plus a few myboard routes.

- **Base URL:** the origin this file was fetched from (for `https://example.com/llms.txt` it is `https://example.com`). Below it is written as `$MB`.
- **Authentication:** send a personal API token on every request: `Authorization: Bearer mbt_...`. A person creates it on the "Integrations" page. The token acts as that person and sees exactly what they see; there is no separate agent account. A token cannot issue or revoke tokens or change people: that is done in the web app.
- **Format:** JSON in and out. Dates of records are UTC strings like `2026-10-16 09:30:00.000Z`. Text fields hold Markdown where noted.

## Who am I

`GET $MB/api/myboard/me` answers the token's own user: `{"id":"k2v7q0ox1lq5fcp","name":"Alex","username":"alex_dev","role":"member"}`. Use this `id` wherever a filter needs "me".

## Data

Each collection is at `$MB/api/collections/<name>/records`.

**projects** — read for members, write for admins only.
- `id`, `name` (1–60 chars), `key` (2–10 chars, `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+$`, prefix of task numbers, e.g. `MYB`), `description` (≤500), `members` (user ids), `archived` (bool), `color` (`#rrggbb`, lowercase, or empty).

**tasks** — read and write for project members and admins.
- `id`, `project` (project id; fixed after creation), `number` (set by the server, unique per project; a task is called `KEY-number`, e.g. `MYB-17`), `title` (1–200 chars), `description` (Markdown, ≤20000), `status` (`backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, `review`, `done`), `priority` (`low`, `normal`, `high`, `urgent`), `assignees` (up to 10 user ids; each one added must be a member of the project; `"assignees+":"ID"` adds one, `"assignees-":"ID"` removes one), `reviewers` (who checks the task in `review`; the same rules as `assignees`, with `"reviewers+"` and `"reviewers-"`), `labels` (label ids of the same project), `due` (`YYYY-MM-DD` or empty), `position` (number; lower is higher in its column), `author` (set by the server), `edited` (set by the server when a person changes the content, not the order; empty until then), `planned`, `started`, `submitted`, `closed` (the dates of the `todo`, `in_progress`, `review` and `done` columns, set by the server: when the task first gets to that column, a column it skips taking the same date; empty again once the task goes back to an earlier column).
- A new task goes to the top of its column. To move a task, PATCH `status` and, if order matters, `position`.

**labels** — per project; members read and write.
- `id`, `project`, `name` (1–24 chars, unique within the project), `color` (`#rrggbb`, lowercase).

**notes** — per project. A new note is personal: only its author sees it. With `shared: true` every project member sees and edits it.
- `id`, `project` (fixed), `title` (1–120), `body` (Markdown, ≤50000), `shared` (bool; only the author or an admin may change it), `position`, `author` (set by the server, fixed), `edited` (as on a task).

**comments** — the discussion under a task; read and write for members of the task's project and admins.
- `id`, `task` (task id, fixed), `body` (Markdown, ≤5000; never just spaces; may be empty: the web app posts a comment of files alone that way and attaches its files right after), `author` (set by the server, fixed), `created`, `updated`.
- Only the author edits a comment; the author or an admin deletes it. Deleting a task deletes its comments.
- To mention someone who sees the task (a project member or an admin), write `[@Name](user:USER_ID)`: they get notified, and the site shows their current name.

**reactions** — emoji under a comment; read and add for members of the comment's task's project and admins.
- `id`, `comment` (comment id), `author` (set by the server), `emoji` (one of `+1` 👍, `-1` 👎, `laugh` 😄, `hooray` 🎉, `confused` 😕, `heart` ❤️, `rocket` 🚀, `eyes` 👀, `done` ✅, `thanks` 🙏, `fire` 🔥, `clap` 👏, `hundred` 💯, `thinking` 🤔), `created`, `updated`.
- One of each kind per person and comment: the same again answers 400. A reaction cannot be changed; only its author removes it. Nobody is notified.

**attachments** — files under a task's description or in a comment; read and add for members of the task's project and admins.
- `id`, `task` (task id), `comment` (comment id; empty for the description), `file` (the stored name), `name` (the name it came with), `size` (bytes), `author` (the last three set by the server), `created`, `updated`.
- Up to 50 MB each: pictures, PDF, text and logs, CSV, JSON, office documents, archives, video and audio. The server tells the type by the content; HTML, SVG and programs answer 400.
- Only a comment's author adds files to it. A file cannot be changed; whoever uploaded it or an admin deletes it. Deleting a comment or a task deletes its files.
- Files are protected: a link to one carries a file token that lives 3 minutes (see Recipes).

**users** — read for anyone signed in; managed in the web app.
- `id`, `name`, `username` (Telegram), `role` (`admin` or `member`), `deleted` (bool).

## Queries

List requests take these query parameters (URL-encode them, e.g. with `curl -G --data-urlencode`):
- `filter` — e.g. `project.key = "MYB" && status != "done"`. Operators: `=`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `~` (contains), `?=` (any item of a list matches; for list relations name the id: `labels.id ?= "LABEL_ID"`, `assignees.id ?= "USER_ID"`), `&&`, `||`, parentheses. Use literal ids in filters; `@request.auth` is not allowed there.
- `sort` — fields, `-` for descending: `sort=status,position` or `sort=-updated`. `status` sorts by its name, alphabetically.
- `expand` — inline related records: `expand=project,assignees,reviewers,labels`.
- `page`, `perPage` (default 30, max 1000).

A list answers `{"page":1,"perPage":30,"totalItems":2,"totalPages":1,"items":[...]}`. Records you may not see are simply absent from lists.

Send changes one request at a time: `/api/batch` accepts only `position` changes (the board's reordering).

## Recipes

Set `MB` and `TOKEN` first. Every command below was run against a real instance.

```sh
MB=https://example.com
TOKEN=mbt_...
auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN")
```

My open tasks across all projects (as an assignee or a reviewer), with their project:

```sh
ME=$(curl -s "${auth[@]}" "$MB/api/myboard/me" | jq -r .id)
curl -sG "${auth[@]}" "$MB/api/collections/tasks/records" \
  --data-urlencode "filter=(assignees.id ?= \"$ME\" || reviewers.id ?= \"$ME\") && status != \"done\"" \
  --data-urlencode 'expand=project' --data-urlencode 'sort=status,position'
```

Projects I can see (not archived):

```sh
curl -sG "${auth[@]}" "$MB/api/collections/projects/records" --data-urlencode 'filter=archived = false'
```

Find task MYB-17:

```sh
curl -sG "${auth[@]}" "$MB/api/collections/tasks/records" \
  --data-urlencode 'filter=project.key = "MYB" && number = 17'
```

Create a task (the answer contains its `number`):

```sh
curl -s "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$MB/api/collections/tasks/records" \
  -d '{"project":"PROJECT_ID","title":"Add a backup check","description":"Restore the latest backup into a scratch instance once a week.","status":"todo","priority":"high"}'
```

Move a task, assign it, set a due date (send only the fields you change):

```sh
curl -s "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X PATCH "$MB/api/collections/tasks/records/TASK_ID" \
  -d '{"status":"in_progress","assignees+":"USER_ID","due":"2026-10-30"}'
```

People to assign (members of a project are its `members` ids):

```sh
curl -sG "${auth[@]}" "$MB/api/collections/users/records" --data-urlencode 'filter=deleted = false'
```

Labels of a project, and a new one:

```sh
curl -sG "${auth[@]}" "$MB/api/collections/labels/records" --data-urlencode 'filter=project.key = "MYB"'
curl -s "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$MB/api/collections/labels/records" \
  -d '{"project":"PROJECT_ID","name":"backend","color":"#3b82f6"}'
```

Write a note and share it with the project:

```sh
curl -s "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$MB/api/collections/notes/records" \
  -d '{"project":"PROJECT_ID","title":"Release checklist","body":"- backup\n- migrate\n- smoke test"}'
curl -s "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X PATCH "$MB/api/collections/notes/records/NOTE_ID" \
  -d '{"shared":true}'
```

Read the discussion of a task and reply to it:

```sh
curl -sG "${auth[@]}" "$MB/api/collections/comments/records" \
  --data-urlencode 'filter=task = "TASK_ID"' --data-urlencode 'sort=created' --data-urlencode 'expand=author'
curl -s "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$MB/api/collections/comments/records" \
  -d '{"task":"TASK_ID","body":"Done, needs a review."}'
```

React to a comment, and take the reaction back:

```sh
curl -s "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$MB/api/collections/reactions/records" \
  -d '{"comment":"COMMENT_ID","emoji":"+1"}'
curl -s "${auth[@]}" -X DELETE "$MB/api/collections/reactions/records/REACTION_ID"
```

Attach a file to a task's description (add `-F comment=COMMENT_ID` for a comment of yours), then download one:

```sh
curl -s "${auth[@]}" -X POST "$MB/api/collections/attachments/records" -F task=TASK_ID -F file=@screenshot.png
FILE_TOKEN=$(curl -s "${auth[@]}" -X POST "$MB/api/files/token" | jq -r .token)
curl -s -o report.pdf "$MB/api/files/attachments/ATTACHMENT_ID/STORED_FILE_NAME?token=$FILE_TOKEN"
```

Delete a task: `curl -s "${auth[@]}" -X DELETE "$MB/api/collections/tasks/records/TASK_ID"` (answers 204, cannot be undone).

## Errors

Errors answer `{"status":400,"message":"...","data":{...}}`.
- **400** — invalid data; `data` names each field, e.g. `{"title":{"code":"validation_required","message":"Cannot be blank."}}`, or `validation_not_unique` for a label name already used in the project. Also a create the token's user is not allowed to make (a task in someone else's project).
- **401** — the token is missing, wrong or revoked.
- **403** — not allowed with a token or in a filter: issuing or revoking tokens, changing people, `@request` in `filter`.
- **404** — the record does not exist **or** you may not see or change it; the API does not tell the two apart.
- **429** — too many requests: at most 300 requests per 10 s and 20 creates per 5 s from one client. Wait and retry.

## Good manners

- Read before you write: look up ids by key, number or name instead of guessing.
- Change only what you were asked to; PATCH only the fields you change.
- Keep titles short; put details in `description` as Markdown.
- Personal notes are private. Do not share a note unless asked.
